  "reasons": [
    "Under the fixed capital method, partners' capital accounts always show a credit balance and remain fixed year after year unless capital is introduced or withdrawn by agreement.",
    "Items like drawings, interest, and share of profit or loss are recorded in current accounts, not capital accounts.",
    "Current accounts can show a debit or a credit balance, and a debit balance is shown on the assets side of the balance sheet."
  ],
  "syllabus_chapter": "Partnership Fundamentals",
  "syllabus_topic": "Fixed v/s Fluctuating Capital",

    {
      "condition": "The partnership maintains capitals under the fixed capital method.",
      "status": "explicit",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    }
  ],
  "option_challenges": [
    {
      "option": "A",

      "correct_under_reading": false,

    },
    {

      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E1.1",
      "premise_quote": "All items like share of profit or loss, interest on capital, drawings, interest on drawings, etc. are recorded in a separate accounts, called Partner’s Current Account.",
      "reason": "These adjustments are recorded in current accounts, not capital accounts."
    },
    {
      "option": "B",
      "status": "supported",
      "false_part": "",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E1.1",
      "premise_quote": "The partners’ capital accounts will always show a credit balance, which shall remain the same (fixed) year after year unless there is any addition or withdrawal of capital.",
      "reason": "Accurately describes capital accounts under the fixed capital method."
    },
    {
      "option": "C",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Current accounts always show a credit balance",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E1.1",
      "premise_quote": "The partners’ current account on the other hand, may show a debit or a credit",
